name: Historic District
tagline: The twenty-two squares under live oaks and Spanish moss
description: The 1733 grid of squares that makes Savannah what it is, each one a small park shaded by live oaks, surrounded by antebellum townhouses now holding the art school, the museums and the restaurants. It is the largest National Historic Landmark District in the country and among the most walkable places in America.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the squares, the restaurants and the river on foot
pros: Twenty-two squares and the whole district walkable
Restaurants, bars and museums all close
No car needed if you stay inside it
cons: The highest rents in the city
Very busy with visitors and tour trolleys

name: Starland District
tagline: The converted southern quarter, murals and new restaurants
description: A district south of Forsyth Park that was industrial and neglected and has been converted over the last decade into the city's creative quarter, with murals, converted warehouses, breweries and the newer restaurants. It is where the art school graduates who stay tend to end up.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting the newer restaurants and a creative neighbourhood
pros: The most interesting new restaurants and bars
Murals and a genuine creative community
cons: Redevelopment is uneven street by street
Ten to fifteen minutes from the squares
Some blocks still require caution after dark

name: Ardsley Park
tagline: The 1910s residential suburb, brick houses and big trees
description: A planned early-twentieth-century neighbourhood south of Forsyth, with brick and stucco houses on tree-lined streets around small parks. It is quiet, settled and the most comfortable residential area in the city, a short drive or a long walk from downtown, and popular with families.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a quiet house and a settled neighbourhood
pros: Quiet, safe and shaded residential streets
cons: Nothing walkable beyond the neighbourhood itself

name: Tybee Island (30 km east)
tagline: The beach, half an hour down the road
description: Savannah's beach, a barrier island thirty kilometres east with three miles of sand, a lighthouse, a fort and a small permanent community of a few thousand. It is a separate place with a different pace, busy in summer and quiet the rest of the year, and it is where Savannah goes on a hot weekend.
bestFor: Stays that want the beach and are content to drive into the city
pros: Three miles of Atlantic beach at the door
Its own bars, restaurants and lighthouse
cons: Thirty to forty minutes into Savannah
Hurricane exposure is real on a barrier island

name: Midtown and the Southside
tagline: Where most of Savannah lives, and where rents make sense
description: The residential and commercial districts spreading south along Abercorn, with the malls, the supermarkets, the hospitals and ordinary American suburban housing. It has none of the charm and all of the practicality, and it is where a long stay stops being expensive.
bestFor: Longer stays where the Historic District rents are prohibitive
pros: Rents well below the historic core
